name: MQTT Client Component
description: The MQTT Client Component sets up the MQTT connection to your broker. If you are connecting to Home Assistant, you may prefer to use the native API, in which case this is not needed.

config_entries.label: Password
config_entries.description: The password to use for authentication. Empty (the default) means no authentication.

config_entries.label: Broker
config_entries.description: The host of your MQTT broker.

config_entries.label: Username
config_entries.description: The username to use for authentication. Empty (the default) means no authentication.

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Birth Message
config_entries.description: The message to publish once connected to the broker.

config_entries.label: Payload
config_entries.description: The message content. Will be filled by the actual payload with some options, like log_topic.

config_entries.label: Topic
config_entries.description: The MQTT topic to publish the message.

config_entries.label: QOS
config_entries.description: The Quality of Service level of the topic. Defaults to 0.

config_entries.label: Retain
config_entries.description: If the published message should have a retain flag on or not. Defaults to true.

config_entries.label: Certificate Authority
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32. CA certificate in PEM format, used instead of the certificate bundle. See [TLS (ESP32)](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt/#mqtt-tls-idf).

config_entries.label: Clean Session
config_entries.description: Whether the broker will clean the MQTT session after disconnect. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Client Certificate
config_entries.description:
**Set together with:** `client_certificate_key` (all-or-none).

Only on `esp32`. Client certificate in PEM format.

config_entries.label: Client Certificate Key
config_entries.description:
**Set together with:** `client_certificate` (all-or-none).

Only on `esp32`. Client private key in PEM format.

config_entries.label: Client ID
config_entries.description: The client id to use for opening connections. See [Defaults](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt/#defaults) for more information.

config_entries.label: Discover IP
config_entries.description: If Home Assistant automatic device discovery should be enabled. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Discovery
config_entries.description: Manually enable/disable discovery for a component. Defaults to the global default.

config_entries.label: Discovery Object ID Generator
config_entries.description: The object_id generator to use. Can be one of `none` or `device_name`. Defaults to `none` which does not generate object_id. `device_name` generator uses format `<device_name>_<friendly_name>`.

config_entries.label: Discovery Prefix
config_entries.description: The prefix to use for Home Assistant's MQTT discovery. Should not contain trailing slash. Defaults to `homeassistant`.

config_entries.label: Discovery Retain
config_entries.description: Whether to retain MQTT discovery messages so that entities are added automatically on Home Assistant restart. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Discovery Unique ID Generator
config_entries.description: The unique_id generator to use. Can be one of `legacy` or `mac`. Defaults to `legacy`, which generates unique_id in format `ESP<component_type><default_object_id>`. `mac` generator uses format `<mac_address>-<component_type>-<fnv1_hash(friendly_name)>`.

config_entries.label: Enable On Boot
config_entries.description: If enabled, MQTT will be enabled on boot. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Idf Send Async
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32. If true publishing the message happens from a separate mqtt task. The client only enqueues the message. Defaults to `false`. The advantage of asynchronous publishing is that it doesn't block the esphome main thread for potentially tens of seconds. The disadvantage is additional memory usage for the thread. Set this to true if you need to ensure that mqtt does not block the main thread, especially if you have poor network conditions.

config_entries.label: Keepalive
config_entries.description: The time to keep the MQTT socket alive, decreasing this can help with overall stability due to more WiFi traffic with more pings. Defaults to 15 seconds.

config_entries.label: Log Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to send MQTT log messages to. Use `null` if you want to disable sending logs to MQTT. The `log_topic` has an additional configuration option: When `esphome logs` connects through the broker, the device prints the log of its previous crash, if there is one, as it does for a native API client. It offers this only while `level` lets error messages through.

config_entries.label: Level
config_entries.description: The log level to use for MQTT logs. See [Log Levels](https://esphome.io/components/logger/#log-levels) for options.

config_entries.label: Topic
config_entries.description: The MQTT topic to publish the message.

config_entries.label: QOS
config_entries.description: The Quality of Service level of the topic. Defaults to 0.

config_entries.label: Retain
config_entries.description: If the published message should have a retain flag on or not. Defaults to true.

config_entries.label: Max Payload Size
config_entries.description: The largest incoming message in bytes, from 512 to 1048576; a unit such as `16kB` also works. Longer messages are dropped with a warning in the log. Defaults to `32768` on ESP32, `16384` on BK72xx, RTL87xx and LN882x, and `8192` on ESP8266.

config_entries.label: Persist Subscriptions
config_entries.description: Skip sending the subscriptions again when the device reconnects and the broker still has them from the previous session. This saves traffic and time on each connection, which helps battery-powered and deep sleep devices. Requires `clean_session: false`. Defaults to `false`. The device keeps one fingerprint of its subscriptions (topics, QoS and the configuration) in memory that survives deep sleep and restarts but not a power loss: RTC memory on the ESP8266 and on ESP32 chips that have it. Nothing is written to flash. When the broker reports that the session is still present and the fingerprint matches the one the broker last accepted in full, no subscriptions are sent; otherwise all of them are sent as usual. While they are being sent the fingerprint is not trusted, so a connection lost part way through cannot be mistaken for a complete session. After a power loss, and after any restart on chips without RTC memory (the ESP32-C2 and ESP32-C61 and the LibreTiny chips), the first connection subscribes to everything once. Unsubscribing from a topic at run time also makes the next connection subscribe to everything again. Subscriptions that a lambda adds after the device has connected make the fingerprint differ between restarts and reconnects, so everything is subscribed again then. Topics that only an older firmware used stay subscribed on the broker until it drops the session. To drop them sooner, flash the device once with `clean_session: true` and without `persist_subscriptions`, let it connect, then flash the usual configuration again.

config_entries.label: Port
config_entries.description: The port to connect to. Defaults to `1883`, or `8883` when `tls` is enabled.

config_entries.label: Publish Nan As None
config_entries.description: Publish `None` instead of `NaN` for sensor states, climate target temperatures (both limits of a two-point target) and climate target humidity, so Home Assistant can represent missing values. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Reboot Timeout
config_entries.description: The amount of time to wait before rebooting when no MQTT connection exists. Can be disabled by setting this to `0s`. Defaults to `15min`.

config_entries.label: Shutdown Message
config_entries.description: The message to send when the node shuts down and the connection is closed cleanly. See [Last Will And Birth Messages](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt/#mqtt-last_will_birth) for more information.

config_entries.label: Payload
config_entries.description: The message content. Will be filled by the actual payload with some options, like log_topic.

config_entries.label: Topic
config_entries.description: The MQTT topic to publish the message.

config_entries.label: QOS
config_entries.description: The Quality of Service level of the topic. Defaults to 0.

config_entries.label: Retain
config_entries.description: If the published message should have a retain flag on or not. Defaults to true.

config_entries.label: Skip Cert Cn Check
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32. Don't verify if the common name in the server certificate matches the value of `broker`.

config_entries.label: TLS
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32. Use TLS for the connection. Defaults to `false`; it is switched on when `verify_ssl`, `certificate_authority`, `client_certificate` or `skip_cert_cn_check` is set, and cannot be `false` together with them. See [TLS (ESP32)](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt/#mqtt-tls-idf).

config_entries.label: Topic Prefix
config_entries.description: The prefix used for all MQTT messages. Should not contain trailing slash. Defaults to `<APP_NAME>`. Use `null` to disable publishing or subscribing of any MQTT topic unless it is explicitly configured.

config_entries.label: Transport
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32 with the ESP-IDF framework. How the broker is reached: `tcp` (default), `ws` (MQTT over WebSocket) or `wss` (MQTT over WebSocket with TLS, which switches `tls` on). See [MQTT over WebSocket](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt/#mqtt-over-websocket).

config_entries.label: Use Abbreviations
config_entries.description: Whether to use [Abbreviations](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/mqtt/discovery/) in discovery messages. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Verify SSL
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32. Check the broker's certificate. Defaults to `true`: with `certificate_authority` the broker is checked against that CA, otherwise against ESP-IDF's certificate bundle (the Mozilla root store), which is then included in the build. Set it to `false` for a broker whose certificate cannot be checked at all; this cannot be combined with `certificate_authority` or `skip_cert_cn_check`.

config_entries.label: Wait For Connection
config_entries.description: Blocks other components from starting until the MQTT connection is established. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Will Message
config_entries.description: The last will message the broker publishes when it loses the connection to the device unexpectedly. A clean shutdown publishes `shutdown_message` instead.

config_entries.label: Payload
config_entries.description: The message content. Will be filled by the actual payload with some options, like log_topic.

config_entries.label: Topic
config_entries.description: The MQTT topic to publish the message.

config_entries.label: QOS
config_entries.description: The Quality of Service level of the topic. Defaults to 0.

config_entries.label: Retain
config_entries.description: If the published message should have a retain flag on or not. Defaults to true.

config_entries.label: Ws Path
config_entries.description: Only with `transport: ws` or `wss`. Path of the WebSocket endpoint on the broker. Defaults to `/mqtt`.
